package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion Platform was compromised at the build process, resulting in malicious code being inserted into official software updates. This allowed attackers to distribute backdoored software to thousands of organizations, enabling unauthorized remote access and lateral movement within victim networks.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update installation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code checks the process context and network availability, then sends encoded system information to a hardcoded command-and-control domain, enabling remote attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates unsolicited outbound network connections to an attacker-controlled domain, exfiltrating system information immediately upon service start.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update code should not beacon to external domains or exfiltrate system data during normal operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update-checking code may contact vendor servers, but not unknown or unrelated domains.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial beacon and C2 activation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives commands from the C2 server, executes arbitrary attacker-supplied payloads, and sends the results back to the attacker, enabling remote code execution and lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows remote, unauthenticated execution of arbitrary commands from an external server, which is a hallmark of backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not accept or execute arbitrary code from untrusted remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may execute commands, but only with strong authentication and user consent.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the SolarWinds Orion build process, resulting in backdoored DLLs distributed via official updates.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial compromise of customer environments upon update installation

attack_chain.action: Upon service start, the malicious DLL beacons to the attacker's C2 domain, sending encoded system information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of C2 channel and victim identification

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands via the C2 channel, which are executed on the victim system, enabling lateral movement and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote access and post-exploitation activities

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from SolarWinds Orion processes to avsvmcloud.com or similar domains
SolarWinds Orion DLLs initiating encoded system information beacons at service start
Remote command execution originating from Orion service processes
file_indicators: Unexpected modifications to Orion update files
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP(S) POSTs from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion servers to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Inspect Orion DLLs for unauthorized code changes. Alert on Orion processes executing unexpected child processes or network activity. Correlate update installation events with subsequent suspicious network or process behavior.
